summary: Completed static review of the PHP/MySQL Phase 1 implementation. PHP runtime, MySQL, and credentials were unavailable, so no live endpoint or authentication execution was possible.

critical.issue: PHP is not installed in the test container, so syntax, PDO connectivity, session behavior, and auth flows could not be verified.

minor.issue: Logout is a state-changing GET request without CSRF protection; use POST plus CSRF validation where practical.
Password is accepted as a command-line argument and can be exposed through process listings or shell history.
No visible login throttling or lockout mechanism is present; consider rate limiting for production deployment.

integration_issues.issue: The page loads several hard-coded Marathi labels and calls-to-action (including organization name references), while only a subset of content is loaded from settings. site_sections seed data is not used by the public page.

action_items: Run php -l across every PHP file and execute the API/auth regression flow in a PHP 8 + MySQL 8 environment.
Make public organization/section identity and content come from database settings/site_sections rather than hard-coded markup.
Protect logout with a CSRF-validated POST flow and improve create-admin secret handling.
Add deployment verification for required PHP extensions, database connectivity, HTTPS cookie behavior, and Apache rules.
critical_code_review_comments: config.php uses development defaults including root with an empty password; production setup must fail closed when required configuration is missing.
storage/.htaccess referenced by README/security guidance is absent; ensure storage is outside the document root or explicitly protected.
External Unsplash and Google Fonts assets are not self-hosted and make the first page dependent on third-party availability.
test_credentials: No credentials supplied; /app/memory/test_credentials.md contains no credentials.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PHP binary is unavailable in this container. Re-run from a PHP 8/MySQL 8 host after addressing dynamic-content and deployment findings.
rca of the issue: The implementation statically renders public labels and membership/about copy in index.php instead of querying site_sections; settings updates therefore cannot fully control the public organization experience. Runtime findings remain unverified because the required PHP/MySQL services are absent.
